purpose: Close projection-layer scaffolds without promoting physics or application claims.
core_rule: Projection is extraction from lawful residue-conditioned closure, not proof of external identity.

projection_signature.definition: A domain-specific pattern extracted from <->_R-supported process closure.
projection_signature.formal_candidate: Sig_app(X) := Extract_X(A <->_R B | R_trace, O, T)
projection_signature.governance: QM_app and GR_app signatures are projection classes, not physical equivalence claims.

orientation_space.definition: The admissible space of orientation or tuning conditions over an RT-expression field.
orientation_space.formal_candidate: O := { -(i)_k | -(i)_k preserves typed admissible continuation under delta_a }
orientation_space.transport_rule: NavT: O_k x R_<-> x A_adm x T -> O_{k+1}
orientation_space.equivalence_rule: -(i)_a ~_O -(i)_b iff they preserve the same admissible closure class under bounded deformation.
orientation_space.failure_rule: orientation transport fails when no admissible O_{k+1} preserves closure support.

topology_to_geometry.definition: Projection operator mapping stabilized topology signatures into metric-readable geometry_app.
topology_to_geometry.warning: Geo_app is not physical spacetime unless empirical mapping standards are satisfied.

empirical_mapping_standards.definition: Rules for translating internal framework projections into external measurement language.
forbidden_without_EMS: claiming G, h, or c derivation

iff_s.definition: Statistical projection operator mapping mismatch or intensity structures into probability-like realization language.
iff_s.failure_rule: <->_s is undefined when event classes, normalization, or admissibility support are missing.

otimes.definition: Composite directional coupling operator joining admissibility-forward and residue-support phases without collapsing them.
otimes.reading: lawful continuation selected forward under delta_a while supported backward by residue trace.
otimes.composition_rule: (A ->_a B) otimes (B <-_r A) is valid iff continuation and support preserve typed nonzero distinction.
